tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

kawchak-resnet50-nontrainable: Figure 1a caption, p.1: the paper labels its own ResNet50 as 23M non-trainable parameters.
kawchak-4qubit-hybrid-setup: Synopsis, p.1: the paper states its own model, circuit size, metrics and the three datasets.
kawchak-circuit-layout-40-params: Figure 1b caption, p.1: states the circuit layout and up to 40 trainable parameters.
kawchak-three-datasets: Figure 1c caption, p.1: lists the three datasets; references 4 to 6 name their sources.
kawchak-simulator-and-gpu: Footer line, p.1: names Default.qubit and the V100 16 GB with reference numbers 13 and 14. A bare footer, but it names the study's device and hardware; the sibling Kawchak paper confirms Default.qubit.
kawchak-ry-layers-quantum-transfer-learn: Introduction, p.2: states what the study varies (trainable Ry layers in a quantum transfer learning model) and why.
kawchak-run-setup-epochs-credits: Table 1 footer, p.1: states 10 epochs, High RAM and the Colab credits per hour for each compute method.
kawchak-colab-rate-and-simulator: Table 1 footer, p.1: states the $0.100 per credit rate and that the QTL model uses the Default.qubit simulator. Hourly rates in the headers equal credits per hour times $0.100, so it is consistent.
kawchak-hourly-rates: Table 1 column headers, p.1: each compute method's hourly rate is stated.
kawchak-cost-efficiency-definition: Table 1 headers, p.1: cost is Runtime*Rate and efficiency is 1/(Runtime*Cost). The efficiency header wraps across two lines in the text layer; table values fit it (0.143 Hr, $0.003 gives 2331).
kawchak-tl-2class-setup: Table 1 first block heading, p.1: states the model, dataset, batch, image count and train split.
kawchak-qtl-2class-setup: Table 1 second block heading, p.1: states the model, 4 qubit CQD Algorithm A, batch, images and split.
kawchak-tl-44class-setup: Table 1 third block heading, p.1: states the model, dataset, batch, image count and split.
kawchak-qtl-44class-setup: Table 1 fourth block heading, p.1: states the model, 17 qubit CQD Algorithm A, batch, images and split.
kawchak-scope-goal-measurements: Page 3, Goals and Objectives and Measurements: the paper states its own comparison goal and what the runtimes and costs depend on.
setup-spin-boson-model: Section 1, Eqs. 1 to 5, pp.1-2: the paper states the spin-boson model with linear bath coupling as its demonstration system.
setup-pade-pole-cutoff: Section 1, p.2, after Eq. 9: the paper states it adopts Pade pole decomposition and cuts the sum at finite P. The explicit expressions are in the SI, not in the text; the value does not depend on them.
definition-ado-index-set: Section 1, p.2, before Eq. 10: the paper defines the ADO label n as an ordered set of P+1 non-negative integers, each tied to a frequency gamma_p.
heom-truncation-scheme: Section 1, p.2, after Eq. 10: the paper defines the simplest truncation as rho^n = 0 when the sum of n_p exceeds L.
definition-bond-dimension: Section 2, p.4, after Eq. 17: the paper defines the bond dimension D_i and Dmax as the maximum.
definition-ttns-loop-free: Section 2, p.4: the paper describes TTNS as a loop-free tree extension of MPS/TT with a unique path between any two tensors.
ttno-decomposition-super-hamiltonian: Section 2, pp.4-5, Eqs. 19 to 22: the paper defines the TTNO form of H with the TTNS structure and the 4x4x4 connecting tensor WX with explicit entries.
tdvp-sweep-procedure: Section 3, p.6: the paper defines its full TDVP step and sweep, starting at a canonicalized TTNS and ending at the root, with the example path for Fig. 1(d).
benchmark-setup-parameters: Section 4, p.6 and Fig. 3 caption: the paper states initial spin-up state and the parameter values.
benchmark-slow-bath-regime: Section 4, p.6: the paper states it chose a much smaller Omega (10 against 50 to 300 cm-1) and calls the bath relaxation slow; the abstract names the same slow-relaxing bath regime. The paper's own statement of the regime it tested.
benchmark-hardware-and-code: Section 4, p.6: the paper states Julia code and a single CPU core of an Apple MacBook Pro with M1 chip.
conventional-code-not-optimized-limit: Section 4, p.6: the paper states its conventional HEOM code is not fully optimized, a caveat on its own speed comparison. The filtering remark is the author's view, but the caveat is stated.
mpo-built-with-itensor: Section 4, pp.6-7: the paper states the MPO for its MPS/TT test came from ITensor.
method-overview: Abstract, p.1 and Section 1: the paper states its own method and what it demonstrates.
design-requirements: Section 2, p.2: the paper states its own two design requirements as bullets.
mqfc-architecture: Section 2, p.2: the paper describes its own m-QFC design with multi-colour pump trains of the same period and relative delays.
comb-pulse-train-generation: Section 2, p.2: the paper states how its pump trains are formed from comb-line subsets; the experiment in Section 3 uses this. The period and width relation is stated, not proved.
ratio-manifold-estimator: Section 2, p.4, Eqs. 1 to 5: the paper defines the ratio vector, the distance function and the arg-min estimate.
estimator-no-timetag-limit: Section 2, p.4 and Section 4, p.10: the paper states twice that the estimator ignores detector time tags and a better method is future work.
exp-comb-and-shaper: Section 3, p.4: the paper states the 25 GHz comb and the Finisar 16000A wave-shaper.
exp-delay-and-fiber: Section 3, p.4: the paper states the delay line in the signal arm and the 10 m fiber in the pump arm.
exp-detection-stage: Section 3, p.4: the paper states the grating spectrograph, three paths, 1 nm filters and three Si-APDs with a time tagger.
exp-throughput-compensation: Section 3, p.4: the paper states that normalized count ratios compensate throughput differences; Eq. 1 defines the normalization.
exp-wavelengths: Section 4, p.5: the paper states the signal, pump and output wavelengths of its run.
exp-pulse-widths: Section 4, p.5: the paper states approximate intensity FWHM widths of 3.8 ps and 12.5 ps.
delay-scan-range: Section 4, p.6: the paper states the scan range of 20 to 60 ps and the shift to a 0 to 40 ps display.
rmse-definition: Section 4, p.8: the paper defines RMSE over the evaluated delay points.
direct-detection-benchmark-definition: Section 4, p.9 and Appendix A: the paper defines the direct-detection reference as jitter over sqrt(N_sig); jitter is measured independently (38.117 ps).

theory_low.schrodinger-like-mapping: Section 1, pp.2-3, Eq. 11 to 14: the mapping to a Schrodinger-like equation is cited from Refs. 29, 31 and 51-56 and is described briefly, not derived or proved here. The paper only uses it.
theory_low.reduced-density-from-ground-state-bath: Section 1, p.3, after Eq. 12: stated as a property of the HEOM construction with no derivation or proof in the paper, and it is an inherited HEOM fact. Not a new definition here.
theory_low.super-hamiltonian-non-hermitian: Section 1, p.3, after Eq. 16: a remark ('worth noting') with no proof. It is a property, not a stated limitation of the work, so 'stated limit' does not fit.
